about: How the lock and a Durable Object compare a migration's text: canonical in engine/migrate/src/lock.rs and its port in src/migration-text.ts, and normalized beside each. Both test suites read every case here, so the two can't drift apart.

canonical.why: Quoted text is kept as written.
A `--` before a tab, or at the end, is a comment everywhere.
A comment Postgres nests and MySQL ends at its first `*/` is kept as written.
A backslash both readings agree on changes nothing.
A space beyond ASCII inside quotes is kept, and spacing outside them is ASCII's alone.
A carriage return before a line feed ends a comment everywhere.
A `[...]` whose quotes close inside it reads as a subscript does.
canonical.sql:
select data['key'],  arr[1] -- c
from t

same.why: Comments and spacing are no edit.

differ.why: A `--` inside a string is no comment.
differ.a: insert into a values ('-- not a comment')

differ.why: MySQL's `\'` is a quote inside the string, so `-- b` is string text there.

differ.a: create table t (a int) /*!50100 PARTITION BY HASH (a) */
differ.b: create table t (a int) /*!50100 PARTITION BY KEY (a) */

differ.why: A comment Postgres nests and MySQL ends at its first `*/`.
differ.a: /* a /* b */ create table t (a int); /* */
differ.b: /* a /* b */ create table t (a bigint); /* */

differ.why: MySQL's `#` comment is an operator to Postgres.
differ.a:
# see reylo/*.sql
create table t (a int);
differ.b:
# see reylo/*.sql
create table t (a bigint);

differ.why: The databases read U+3000 and U+00A0 outside quotes and comments as part of a name.
differ.a: create view v as select 1 as x　, 2 as y;
differ.b: create view v as select 1 as x , 2 as y;

differ.why: MySQL reads `--` before one, or before DEL as the statements are split for it, as `- -` and runs the rest of the line.
A lone carriage return ends a `--` comment on Postgres alone.
A lone carriage return in a string is another value than a line feed.
Postgres takes any character past ASCII in a dollar quote's tag.
A `$` inside a name opens no dollar quote.
SQLite's `[...]` is a name: a quote or a dollar sign inside one opens nothing there.
differ.a: create table t ([$　$] text default 'a $　$ -- one');
differ.b: create table t ([$　$] text default 'a $　$ -- two');

differ.a: create table t ([a'b] text default 'x -- y')
differ.b: create table t ([a'b] text default 'x -- z')

normalized.why: Line endings as line feeds, a lone carriage return kept, and no trailing ASCII spacing.
A space beyond ASCII that ends a file is part of a name.
